stem: The value of determinant \(\begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ -7 & -4 \end{vmatrix}\) is ____.
solution:
**(D)** \(1\)
\(\begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ -7 & -4 \end{vmatrix} = (5)(-4) - (3)(-7) = -20 + 21\).
\(\therefore\) the value of the determinant is \(1\). The value \(-41\) comes from wrongly writing \(-20 - 21\), forgetting that \(-(3)(-7) = +21\).

stem: Out of the following equations which one is not a quadratic equation?
solution:
**(A)** \(x^2 + 4x = 11 + x^2\)
A quadratic equation must have degree \(2\) after simplification. Here \(x^2 + 4x = 11 + x^2 \Rightarrow 4x - 11 = 0\): the \(x^2\) terms cancel and the equation is linear (degree \(1\)).
The others simplify to \(x^2 - 4x = 0\), \(5x^2 - 90 = 0\) and \(2x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0\), each of degree \(2\).
\(\therefore x^2 + 4x = 11 + x^2\) is not a quadratic equation.

**(B)** \(3.5\)
\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\), so \(t_2 = a + d = 3.5 + 0\).
\(\therefore t_2 = 3.5\). With \(d = 0\) every term of the A.P. equals the first term.

stem: From the following numbers which number cannot represent a probability?
solution:
**(B)** \(2.0\)
The probability of any event satisfies \(0 \le P(A) \le 1\). The numbers \(0.6\), \(0.15\) and \(0.75\) lie between \(0\) and \(1\), but \(2.0 > 1\).
\(\therefore 2.0\) cannot represent a probability.

stem: For simultaneous equations in variables \(x\) and \(y\), \(D_x = 49\), \(D_y = -63\), \(D = 7\), then find the value of \(x\).
solution:
By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{D_x}{D} = \dfrac{49}{7}\).
\(\therefore x = 7\).

stem: Write the following quadratic equation in standard form: \(2y = 10 - y^2\).
solution:
The standard form is \(ay^2 + by + c = 0\).
\(2y = 10 - y^2 \Rightarrow y^2 + 2y - 10 = 0\).
\(\therefore\) the standard form is \(y^2 + 2y - 10 = 0\), with \(a = 1\), \(b = 2\), \(c = -10\).

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Face value of one share is ₹100 and premium is ₹10. Find the market value of the share.
solution:
When a share is at a premium, \(MV = FV + \text{Premium} = 100 + 10\).
\(\therefore\) the market value of the share is ₹110.

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem: Find the class mark of the class 6–10.
solution:
Class mark \(= \dfrac{\text{lower limit} + \text{upper limit}}{2} = \dfrac{6 + 10}{2} = \dfrac{16}{2}\).
\(\therefore\) the class mark is \(8\).

subtopic: Solving by Formula and Completing the Square
stem: Complete the following activity to solve the quadratic equation \(x^2 + 8x - 48 = 0\) by completing square method.

Courier service agent charged total ₹590 to courier a parcel from Nashik to Nagpur. In the tax invoice taxable value is ₹500 on which CGST is ₹45 and SGST is ₹45. Complete the following activity to find the rate of GST charged for this service.
solution:
Total GST \(=\) CGST \(+\) SGST
\(= 45 + 45\)
\(= ₹90\)
Rate of GST \(= \dfrac{90}{500} \times 100 = 18\)
\(\therefore\) the rate of GST charged by the agent is \(18\%\).
Check: \(500 + 90 = 590\), the total charged.

stem:
The monthly expenditure of a family on different items is shown in the following table. Complete the following activity to calculate the related central angles.

| Different items | Percentage of expenditure |
|---|---|
| Food | 40 |
| Clothing | 20 |
| Education | 30 |
| Other expenditure | 10 |
| Total | 100 |
solution:
Measure of central angle \(= \dfrac{\text{percentage of expenditure}}{100} \times 360^\circ\).

| Different items | Percentage of expenditure | Measure of central angle |
|---|---|---|
| Food | 40 | \(\dfrac{40}{100} \times 360^\circ = 144^\circ\) |
| Clothing | 20 | \(\dfrac{20}{100} \times 360^\circ = 72^\circ\) |
| Education | 30 | \(\dfrac{30}{100} \times 360^\circ = 108^\circ\) |
| Other expenditure | 10 | \(\dfrac{10}{100} \times 360^\circ = 36^\circ\) |
| Total | 100 | \(360^\circ\) |

Check: \(144 + 72 + 108 + 36 = 360\).

stem: Find the values of \((x + y)\) and \((x - y)\) of the following given simultaneous equations: \(101x + 99y = 501\); \(99x + 101y = 499\).
solution:
\(101x + 99y = 501\) ... (I)
\(99x + 101y = 499\) ... (II)
Adding (I) and (II): \(200x + 200y = 1000 \Rightarrow 200(x + y) = 1000\).
\(\therefore x + y = 5\) ... (III)
Subtracting (II) from (I): \(2x - 2y = 2 \Rightarrow 2(x - y) = 2\).
\(\therefore x - y = 1\) ... (IV)
Check: (III) and (IV) give \(x = 3\), \(y = 2\), and \(101(3) + 99(2) = 303 + 198 = 501\).

stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by factorisation method: \(x^2 - 15x + 54 = 0\).
solution:
\(x^2 - 15x + 54 = 0\)
Split the middle term: \(-9 \times -6 = 54\) and \(-9 - 6 = -15\).
\(x^2 - 9x - 6x + 54 = 0 \Rightarrow x(x - 9) - 6(x - 9) = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 9)(x - 6) = 0\).
\(\therefore x = 9\) or \(x = 6\).
Check: sum of roots \(= 15\) and product \(= 54\), matching the equation.

stem: Which term of the following A.P. is 560? \(2, 11, 20, 29, \ldots\)
solution:
Here \(a = 2\), \(d = 11 - 2 = 9\). Let \(t_n = 560\).
\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d \Rightarrow 560 = 2 + (n - 1)9\)
\(\Rightarrow (n - 1)9 = 558 \Rightarrow n - 1 = 62\)
\(\therefore n = 63\). So 560 is the 63rd term of the A.P.
Check: \(t_{63} = 2 + 62 \times 9 = 2 + 558 = 560\).

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Market value of a share is ₹200. If the brokerage rate is 0.3%, then find the purchase value of the share.
solution:
Brokerage \(= 0.3\%\) of MV \(= \dfrac{0.3}{100} \times 200 = ₹0.60\).
On purchase, brokerage is added to the market value.
Purchase value \(= MV + \text{Brokerage} = 200 + 0.60\).
\(\therefore\) the purchase value of the share is ₹200.60.

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem: If \(\sum f_i d_i = 10{,}000\), \(\sum f_i = 100\) and \(A = 2000\), then find mean \((\bar{x})\).
solution:
By the assumed mean method, \(\bar{d} = \dfrac{\sum f_i d_i}{\sum f_i} = \dfrac{10000}{100} = 100\).
\(\bar{x} = A + \bar{d} = 2000 + 100\).
\(\therefore\) mean \(\bar{x} = 2100\).

stem: In an A.P. sum of three consecutive terms is 27 and their product is 504. Complete the following activity to find the terms.
solution:
Let the three consecutive terms be \(a - d\), \(a\), \(a + d\).
\(\therefore a - d + a + a + d = 27\)
\(\therefore 3a = 27\), so \(a = 9\).
Similarly, \((a - d) \times a \times (a + d) = 504\)
\(\therefore [(9)^2 - d^2] \times 9 = 504\)
\(\therefore (81 - d^2) \times 9 = 504\), so \(81 - d^2 = 56\)
\(\therefore d^2 = 81 - 56 = 25\)
\(\therefore d = \pm 5\)
Putting \(a = 9\) and \(d = 5\), the three consecutive terms are \(4, 9, 14\).
Putting \(a = 9\) and \(d = -5\), the three consecutive terms are \(14, 9, 4\).
Check: \(4 + 9 + 14 = 27\) and \(4 \times 9 \times 14 = 504\).

stem:
A card is drawn from a well shuffled pack of 52 playing cards. Complete the following activity to find the probability of the following events:
(a) A red card
(b) A face card.
solution:
Let S be the sample space. \(\therefore n(S) = 52\).
Event A: card drawn is a red card.
Total red cards \(= 26\) (13 hearts and 13 diamonds).
\(\therefore n(A) = 26\)
\(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)}\) (formula)
\(\therefore P(A) = \dfrac{26}{52} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
Event B: card drawn is a face card.
Total face cards \(= 12\) (king, queen and jack of each of the 4 suits).
\(\therefore n(B) = 12\)
\(P(B) = \dfrac{n(B)}{n(S)}\) (formula)
\(\therefore P(B) = \dfrac{12}{52} = \dfrac{3}{13}\).

stem:
In the following table the yearly investment made by 210 families is given. From this information draw the histogram.

| Investment (Thousand Rupees) | Number of families |
|---|---|
| 10–20 | 30 |
| 20–30 | 50 |
| 30–40 | 60 |
| 40–50 | 55 |
| 50–60 | 15 |
solution:
Total families \(= 30 + 50 + 60 + 55 + 15 = 210\), as given.
The classes are continuous (10-20, 20-30, ...), so the histogram is drawn directly:
1. On the X-axis take the investment (thousand rupees). Scale: 1 cm \(= 10\) thousand rupees; since the first class starts at 10, show a kink (zig-zag) on the X-axis between 0 and 10.
2. On the Y-axis take the number of families. Scale: 1 cm \(= 10\) families.
3. Draw adjacent rectangles with no gaps, each of width one class:

| Class (thousand ₹) | Height of rectangle (families) |
|---|---|
| 10-20 | 30 |
| 20-30 | 50 |
| 30-40 | 60 |
| 40-50 | 55 |
| 50-60 | 15 |

The tallest rectangle is over 30-40 (60 families) and the shortest over 50-60 (15 families).

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Shri Shivajirao has purchased 150 shares of F.V. ₹100, for M.V. of ₹120. Company has paid 7% dividend. Find the rate of return on his investment.
solution:
F.V. \(= ₹100\), M.V. \(= ₹120\), number of shares \(= 150\).
Sum invested \(= 150 \times 120 = ₹18{,}000\).
Dividend per share \(= 7\%\) of F.V. \(= \dfrac{7}{100} \times 100 = ₹7\).
Total dividend \(= 150 \times 7 = ₹1{,}050\).
Rate of return \(= \dfrac{\text{Total dividend}}{\text{Sum invested}} \times 100 = \dfrac{1050}{18000} \times 100 = \dfrac{35}{6}\).
\(\therefore\) the rate of return is \(\dfrac{35}{6}\% = 5.83\%\) (approx.).
Check: the return is below the 7% dividend rate because the share was bought above its face value.

stem: Product of Shraddha's age 2 years ago and 3 years hence is 84. Find her present age.
solution:
Let Shraddha's present age be \(x\) years.
Her age 2 years ago \(= (x - 2)\) years and 3 years hence \(= (x + 3)\) years.
\((x - 2)(x + 3) = 84 \Rightarrow x^2 + x - 6 = 84 \Rightarrow x^2 + x - 90 = 0\)
\(\Rightarrow x^2 + 10x - 9x - 90 = 0 \Rightarrow x(x + 10) - 9(x + 10) = 0 \Rightarrow (x + 10)(x - 9) = 0\)
\(\therefore x = 9\) or \(x = -10\). Age cannot be negative, so \(x = 9\).
\(\therefore\) Shraddha's present age is 9 years.
Check: \(7 \times 12 = 84\).

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations graphically: \(x + y = 6\), \(x - y = 4\).
In an agriculture field the ratio of salary of skilled and unskilled workers is 5 : 4. Total salary of one day of both of them is ₹900. Find daily wages of skilled and unskilled workers.
solution:
Let the daily wages of a skilled worker be ₹\(x\) and of an unskilled worker be ₹\(y\).
Ratio of wages: \(\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{5}{4} \Rightarrow 4x = 5y \Rightarrow 4x - 5y = 0\) ... (I)
Total salary of one day: \(x + y = 900\) ... (II)
Multiply (II) by 5: \(5x + 5y = 4500\) ... (III)
Add (I) and (III): \(9x = 4500 \Rightarrow x = 500\).
Substitute in (II): \(500 + y = 900 \Rightarrow y = 400\).
\(\therefore\) the daily wages of the skilled worker are ₹500 and of the unskilled worker are ₹400.
Check: \(500 : 400 = 5 : 4\) and \(500 + 400 = 900\).

stem:
Two dice are thrown. Find the probability of the following events:
(a) Event A: The sum of the numbers on their upper faces is at least 9.
(b) Event B: The sum of the numbers on their upper faces is divisible by 5.
(c) Event C: The number on the upper face of the first die is greater than the number on the upper face of the second die.
solution:
When two dice are thrown, the sample space S has \(6 \times 6\) outcomes \((1,1), (1,2), \ldots, (6,6)\). \(\therefore n(S) = 36\).
(a) Event A: sum at least 9 (sum 9, 10, 11 or 12).
\(A = \{(3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3), (4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), (6,6)\}\), so \(n(A) = 10\).
\(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{10}{36} = \dfrac{5}{18}\).
(b) Event B: sum divisible by 5 (sum 5 or 10).
\(B = \{(1,4), (2,3), (3,2), (4,1), (4,6), (5,5), (6,4)\}\), so \(n(B) = 7\).
\(P(B) = \dfrac{n(B)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{7}{36}\).
(c) Event C: number on the first die greater than the number on the second.
\(C = \{(2,1), (3,1), (3,2), (4,1), (4,2), (4,3), (5,1), (5,2), (5,3), (5,4), (6,1), (6,2), (6,3), (6,4), (6,5)\}\), so \(n(C) = 15\).
\(\therefore P(C) = \dfrac{n(C)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{15}{36} = \dfrac{5}{12}\).
Check for (c): of the 36 outcomes, 6 are doubles and the other 30 split equally between first greater and second greater, giving 15.

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
In the following frequency distribution table ages of 300 patients and number of patients in a hospital is given. Find the median age of the patients.

| Age (In years) | Number of patients |
|---|---|
| 10–20 | 60 |
| 20–30 | 42 |
| 30–40 | 55 |
| 40–50 | 70 |
| 50–60 | 53 |
| 60–70 | 20 |
solution:
| Age (years) | Number of patients \((f)\) | Cumulative frequency (less than type) |
|---|---|---|
| 10-20 | 60 | 60 |
| 20-30 | 42 | 102 |
| 30-40 | 55 | 157 |
| 40-50 | 70 | 227 |
| 50-60 | 53 | 280 |
| 60-70 | 20 | 300 |

\(N = 300\), so \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 150\). The cumulative frequency just greater than 150 is 157, so the median class is 30-40.
\(L = 30\), \(cf = 102\), \(f = 55\), \(h = 10\).
Median \(= L + \left[\dfrac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f}\right] \times h = 30 + \dfrac{150 - 102}{55} \times 10 = 30 + \dfrac{480}{55} = 30 + \dfrac{96}{11}\)
\(\therefore\) Median \(= 30 + 8.73 = 38.73\) years (approx.).
Check: the value lies inside the median class 30-40.

stem:
Three conditions are given below. Write the quadratic equation for each of them satisfy that condition:
(a) If discriminant \(\Delta = 0\)
(b) If discriminant \(\Delta > 0\)
(c) If discriminant \(\Delta < 0\)
solution:
For \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), the discriminant is \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\).
(a) \(\Delta = 0\): take \(x^2 - 4x + 4 = 0\). Here \(a = 1\), \(b = -4\), \(c = 4\), so \(\Delta = (-4)^2 - 4(1)(4) = 16 - 16 = 0\). The roots are real and equal (\(x = 2, 2\)).
(b) \(\Delta > 0\): take \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\). Here \(a = 1\), \(b = -5\), \(c = 6\), so \(\Delta = (-5)^2 - 4(1)(6) = 25 - 24 = 1 > 0\). The roots are real and unequal (\(x = 2, 3\)).
(c) \(\Delta < 0\): take \(x^2 + x + 1 = 0\). Here \(a = 1\), \(b = 1\), \(c = 1\), so \(\Delta = (1)^2 - 4(1)(1) = 1 - 4 = -3 < 0\). The roots are not real.
\(\therefore x^2 - 4x + 4 = 0\), \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\) and \(x^2 + x + 1 = 0\) satisfy the three conditions respectively.

subtopic: Sum of n Terms of an A.P.
stem: If first term of an A.P. is 'p', second term is 'q' and last term is 'r', then show that the sum of all terms is \(\dfrac{(p + r)(q + r - 2p)}{2(q - p)}\).
solution:
First term \(a = p\), second term \(t_2 = q\), so the common difference \(d = q - p\).
Let the A.P. have \(n\) terms, with last term \(t_n = r\).
\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d \Rightarrow r = p + (n - 1)(q - p)\)
\(\Rightarrow n - 1 = \dfrac{r - p}{q - p} \Rightarrow n = \dfrac{r - p}{q - p} + 1 = \dfrac{r - p + q - p}{q - p} = \dfrac{q + r - 2p}{q - p}\).
Sum of \(n\) terms when the first and last terms are known: \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(t_1 + t_n) = \dfrac{n}{2}(p + r)\).
\(\therefore S_n = \dfrac{q + r - 2p}{2(q - p)} \times (p + r) = \dfrac{(p + r)(q + r - 2p)}{2(q - p)}\).
Hence the sum of all terms is \(\dfrac{(p + r)(q + r - 2p)}{2(q - p)}\).
Check with the A.P. \(1, 3, 5\) (\(p = 1\), \(q = 3\), \(r = 5\)): \(\dfrac{(6)(6)}{2(2)} = 9 = 1 + 3 + 5\).
